title: Information Intermediary or De Facto Standard Setter? Field Evidence on the Indirect and Direct Influence of Proxy Advisors

scopes.description: Complete author-documented qualitative interview workflow, including preparation of the de-identified interview corpus and NVivo-assisted manual coding. Historical IRB approval, recruitment, consent, interviews, transcription, and transcription verification are not treated as live execution dependencies for auditing a released prepared corpus.

requirements.description: Author-prepared, de-identified and verified qualitative interview corpus used in the paper: interviews with 37 board directors, HR executives, and compensation consultants, plus six interviews involving eight proxy-advisor representatives. The corpus must include transcripts for recorded interviews and the detailed notes for the five participants who declined recording.

issues.description: The supplied release contains no executable author program. The datasheet explicitly says no program or code was used for the qualitative analysis; the documented manual/GUI coding workflow remains only partially specified.

The release contains no interview transcripts or notes, NVivo project, codebook, coding matrix, coded export, or complete manual coding/reconciliation recipe. Appendix A supplies only customized sample questions; Appendix B contains selected indicative quotations, not the full corpus or analytic record. Current retention and lawful sharing conditions remain unverified.

The six-year retention statement is historical and does not prove that materials are still retained or were deleted. The consent form promises reasonable confidentiality efforts but does not establish that de-identified interview materials cannot be shared; present access permission under the consent and IRB terms needs confirmation.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes 37 compensation-professional interviews and six interviews with eight proxy-advisor representatives, conducted from July 2016 to April 2018.
evidence.quote:
Specifically, we conducted 37 interviews with board directors, HR executives, and compensation
consultants—this is the primary set of interviews on which we draw in the manuscript. In addition,
we conducted six interviews with eight representatives from proxy advisory firms. All of the
interviews occurred between July 2016 and April 2018.

evidence.description: The authors describe the NVivo-assisted coding sequence and report having access to recordings, transcriptions, and qualitative analysis files at the time of the datasheet.
evidence.quote:
With respect to our data analysis, we employed qualitative data analysis software (NVivo). Both authors and a research assistant coded the first five interviews independently. Once we felt
comfortable with our coding scheme, the interviews were coded by the RA and one of the authors. Both authors have access to all digital recordings, all transcriptions, and our qualitative data
analysis files.

evidence.description: The authors explicitly report that no program or code was used for qualitative analysis.
evidence.quote:
NVivo, a qualitative data analysis software
package, was used to facilitate data analysis, but no program or code was used for the analysis.

evidence.description: The datasheet records historical IRB, recruitment, consent, interviewing, transcription, and transcription-verification steps. These are not assumed to be live dependencies when auditing a supplied prepared corpus.
evidence.quote:
a. Obtain approval from our Universities’ Institutional Review Boards (IRB / Office
for the Protection of Research Subjects).
b. Recruit interview participants.
c. Obtain informed consent from each participant.
d. Conduct interview by phone and obtain audio recording (except when a participant
preferred to not be recorded, in which case detailed handwritten notes were taken).
e. Obtain professional transcription of the interview.
f. Verify and correct transcription based on original audio recording (usually
performed by a research assistant).

actions.description: Request the current author-prepared de-identified corpus and qualitative analysis materials, together with the actual manual/GUI coding protocol and NVivo compatibility details, subject to the participants’ consent and applicable IRB terms.
steps: Confirm whether the author-prepared, de-identified corpus still exists; identify the interviews actually used in the paper; provide verified transcripts for recorded sessions and the detailed notes for the five participants who declined recording; and describe current retention status.

Confirm the lawful access and sharing conditions under the participant consent and applicable IRB terms. The confidentiality language does not by itself establish either permission or a categorical bar to sharing de-identified materials.

If retained and shareable, provide the NVivo project or compatible coded export, code definitions/codebook or documented coding scheme, coding matrix or coded segments, and the actual steps for independent initial coding, final coding, and resolution of coding differences.

Specify NVivo version, project/export format, any manual lookup or crosswalk inputs, and the human coding workflow needed to obtain the reported outputs. Verify current software access rather than assuming a license is present.

If the corpus or coding files are unavailable or cannot be shared, document that limitation and provide the most complete non-identifying prepared coding outputs and manual workflow description that may be shared. Do not recruit participants again or infer the full dataset from published excerpts.
validation: Verify that the permitted prepared corpus covers all interviews the authors actually analyzed and distinguishes transcripts from notes for unrecorded participants.
Verify that the supplied coding records and manual protocol identify the analytical units, code definitions, coder assignments, reconciliation rules, and outputs reported in the paper.
Confirm the supplied NVivo project/export opens in the specified software version or in a documented compatible format, and that the named current access route is available.

review_notes: The assigned package root contains only the datasheet and online appendix. It has no author program, transcripts, notes, NVivo project, codebook, coding matrix, or coded export. The datasheet explicitly says no program or code was used; the documented NVivo and human coding procedure is credited as a workflow, but it is not a supplied executable program or complete manual recipe.

Appendix A is a sample question list customized by interview role and prior information. Appendix B supplies selected indicative excerpts. Neither is the complete interview corpus or a substitute for the coding record.

The six-year retention assurance is historical and does not establish current retention, access, or deletion. Consent confidentiality language does not automatically prove sharing impossible; lawful current access to de-identified materials remains unverified.

Historical IRB approval, recruitment, informed consent, conducting new interviews, transcription, and transcription verification are not proposed as live execution dependencies for auditing an author-prepared corpus. Original recordings are not independently demanded if authors can supply their verified analysis corpus and notes.
